You take on the role of a houseplant enthusiast trying to create the coziest interior space by collecting and arranging houseplants and other objects within your home. You must position your plants so that they are provided the most suitable light conditions and take care of them to create the most verdant collection. Each turn, you will select an adjacent pair of a card and token, and use those items to build an ever-expanding tableau of cards - your home. You will need to keep various objectives in mind as you attempt to increase plant verdancy by making spatial matches and using item tokens to take various nurture actions. You will also build your ‘green thumb’ skills allowing you to take additional actions to take care of your plants and create the coziest space! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary In Verdant, players collect plants, room cards, pets and furniture to set up their home to be the coziest, most verdant and to score the most points. Players draft cards and tokens to build out a 3X5 grid of cards alternating between plant cards which need to gain verdancy, and room cards where they can place furniture and pets to score points. Each turn, players select a token/card pair to draft, add the card to their tableau, and use the token (see below). Players begin with a random plant and room card, and will draft 13 more cards. The game ends when everyone has completed their grid. Contents 1 Scoring 1.1 Complete Plants 1.2 Rooms and items 2 How green thumbs work 3 How Nurture Item Tokens work Scoring These are the ways to score points: Complete Plants Plants have a type, light requirements, verdancy requirement, and number of points they score if completed. When placed into the grid the primary goal is to get the plant the verdancy it needs to be completed. Earning verdancy is tracked on the plant cards with verdancy tokens - the light colored ones represent 1 verdancy and the darker ones represent 3 verdancy. Plants can gain verdancy by: • Making one of the three different light requirement matches (low light, medium light, bright light) between a plant card and a room card. This can be made when placing a room card, or when placing a plant card. Each time a match is made, verdancy is added to the plant. • Using Nurture tokens gained in the draft. The bag of fertilizer allows a player to add three verdancy to one single plant, the hand trowel allows a player to add one verdancy to up to three different plants, and the water can allows a player to add verdancy to all plants surrounding a chosen room. • Using green thumbs, (see below). Once a plant is completed a pot will be added! Pots are worth a different number of victory points (1, 2, 3 points), depending on how early they are achieved, so the faster a player completes plants, the more bonuses they will get. Once a plant is potted, it will no longer gain verdancy. If a player does not finish a plant, the verdancy on incomplete plants will score one point for every two verdancy. Rooms and items In addition to providing light to plants, each room also has a wallpaper type that matches one of the plant types. Each room card will score 1 point for each plant of the matching type (up to 4 points). Additionally, if a player adds a token (furnishing or animal) with the same wallpaper type on it onto the room card, it doubles the number of points that room will score for each adjacent plant (up to 8 points, if all adjacent plants match the room with a matching cat or sofa, etc). The furnishings and pets not only add to the room scoring but also score as sets of unique items. [Rating: 1/10] This is probably close to a 5, but the rating for this is just too high. The game looks good and the theme is good, but the game is just meh. I have played it 3 times, once without objective cards and twice with. The cards just don't really feel like a goal as you are likely to lose more points by trying to go for them rather than being more efficient which just makes them more random points people get. I have played both Calico and Cascadia, both of those are just better games that feel better to play.

[Rating: 1/10] Retail got this earlier then the "beloved" backers who helped realizing this project in first place. Would have been fine if open communicated but Was Not the case. Ah and the game is rather blend. Rating fits Company and game a like

[Rating: 1/10] Alright card laying puzzle driven by a novel drafting system with a couple clever quirks to it that's otherwise let down by being too much of a point salad to lend itself to intriguing decisions and interesting play.

[Rating: 1/10] Not a fan. It goes on too long for what it is and the end game feels like a slog of suboptimal decisions to fill out the card grid. Some compared it to Cascadia/Harmonies/Calico. It reminds me more of Kanagawa with the card tableau and icon matching mechanics. Unlike Kanagawa which is a relaxed game, this felt fussy and more effort than its complexity merits.

[Rating: 2/10] the best part of this game is filling in plant conditions and the satisfaction of being able to put a pot tile on them and score, which, if the items don't flop any greens can be quite hard to do            a majority of points are more tied to rooms and matching items...           they really should've focused on the plants aspect of the game but that would've been a completely different game.

[Rating: 2/10] not my type of game, endless drafting and little placement optimizations without any tension or arc. much prefer calico, or even kingdomino

[Rating: 3/10] Backed the KS, played it, traded it, and now played it on BGA. The art and theme is beautiful but the game itself feels needlessly restictive. Every game leaves an unsatisfying feeling when I'm done. The green thumbs and how to use them feels strict and unfun. The storage limit is restictive and lame. Also the placing pets in specific rooms feels odd.   I so wanted to love this game but it is just bleh.

[Rating: 3/10] Way more fiddly than calico and Cascadia. Very long downtime because you can't plan ahead of your turn  Weakest of the 3 by a long shot as decisions feel very random compared to the others in the series

[Rating: 3/10] The game is very repetitive and monotonous. It does not help that the group I was with made this game take over an hour and a half.
